## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

RaceRepositoryImpl — core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/race/RaceRepositoryImpl.kt

## Trigger

None — this is not a missing call but a failure-conversion defect on every
suspend surface of the three Room-backed repositories: RaceRepositoryImpl
(setAsReference, rename, delete, saveImportedRace, saveRecordedRace,
findById, replaceReference), ProfileRepositoryImpl —
core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/profile/ProfileRepositoryImpl.kt
(updateHrMaxBpm, updateZoneThreshold, updateExpectedDistanceM,
updateLongPressMs, updateCorrectionFactor, markSyncSuccess,
applyIncomingProfile), and RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl —
app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt
(startClock, markSegment, findInProgress, undoLastMark, stopRace,
markSent, eraseRecorded) — nothing observes anything; the defect is
reached on every call, not on an event.

## Today

Every suspend surface of the three repositories wraps its `raceDao` /
`profileDao` body in `withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { runCatching { … } }`
and returns the resulting `Result`. `runCatching` catches whatever the
DAO raises — a Room-thrown `android.database.sqlite.SQLiteException`
among them — and wraps it unconverted as the `Result`'s failure cause;
the caller-visible `Result.failure` carries that dependency exception
by value instead of a type the module declares. `RaceRepositoryImpl`
itself already shows the correct shape for its two Flow-returning
methods: `observeAll()` and `observeReference()` catch the flow's
upstream failure and re-emit it as `RaceQueryFailure`
(core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/race/RaceQueryFailure.kt),
a type `:core-domain` declares. The suspend methods in the same file,
and every suspend method of `ProfileRepositoryImpl` and
`RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl`, do not perform the equivalent
conversion — `runCatching` satisfies R31's requirement that no thrown
exception cross the boundary, but the exception still crosses,
transported inside the `Result.failure`'s cause chain.

## Expected

Every suspend surface of `RaceRepositoryImpl`, `ProfileRepositoryImpl`
and `RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl` converts a caught dependency failure
into a declared domain failure type before returning it in `Result.failure`
— the same discipline `RaceQueryFailure` already applies to
`observeAll()` and `observeReference()`. This requires one declared
failure type per repository (or one shared across the three, if the
domain layer accepts a single kind of "store failure"), and every
`runCatching { … }` block's caught throwable wrapped in it — not
returned as-is. A repository's own domain-refusal exceptions (e.g.
`NoSuchElementException` for "no race with id", `IllegalArgumentException`
for a name or bound violation) are equally in scope: today they too cross
as raw JDK exception types inside the `Result`, not as a type the module
declares.
